scope: Finite declared ecology E=(D_tau,O,A,F,V,p,b,H,Delta) extending ECOLOGY_CONTRACT_V1.json + ECOLOGY_AXES_V2.json + DEFINITIONS_V2_EXACT.md s2. Admissibility only (DU-1); every coordinate mechanically checkable before protected outcomes.

other_agents.definition: Explicit other-agent set with declared adaptivity (NONE / FIXED_OPPONENTS / ADAPTIVE_OPPONENTS / COOPERATIVE_TEAM / MIXED_POPULATION) and their observation/action interfaces. Adaptive agents are part of E, not an external bolt-on.
other_agents.parent: TOM-1 opponent-type forcing; GG41 strategic refinement strictly refines single-agent quotient
other_agents.falsifier: a two-agent ecology with ADAPTIVE_OPPONENTS on which a single-agent quotient predicts the frontier yet the adaptive opponent induces a different optimal morphology (TOM-1 forcing violated)

observation_structure.definition: Registered observation alphabet O and mapping obs: WorldState -> O exposed before each decision/update; declares what is observable, with what noise/partial observability, and what is hidden.
observation_structure.parent: POMDP observation model; HST-T03 representation insufficiency
observation_structure.falsifier: an ecology where a strictly larger O is claimed to need no additional state yet the semantic quotient refines on the larger O (undisclosed observation dependence)

action_intervention_structure.definition: Registered action/intervention alphabet A and effect law action: (WorldState, A) -> WorldState distribution; includes legal interventions on ecology variables, not just environment outputs.
action_intervention_structure.parent: Pearl do-calculus / intervention semantics; LMT complete-view lemma on admissible interventions
action_intervention_structure.falsifier: a claimed intervention-free optimum that is beaten by an admitted intervention under the same O and V

feedback_verifier_structure.definition: Development feedback channel F (labels, rewards, checker traces, intervention outcomes) and verifier contract V (membership / equivalence oracle / proof checker) with their availability schedule over H.
feedback_verifier_structure.parent: Angluin 1987 L* vs Gold 1978 passive-intractability; ECOLOGY_AXES_V2 verification_strength axis
feedback_verifier_structure.falsifier: a morphology claimed to develop under passive examples alone on a class whose passive intractability is parent-proved (Gold/Pitt-Warmuth/Kearns-Valiant)

task_distribution_horizon.definition: Finite registered task family D_tau and horizon H (task count / reuse opportunities / time steps); the distribution is over tasks, not just samples within a task.
task_distribution_horizon.parent: Shalev-Shwartz comp-stat tradeoff; task-diversity / curriculum literature
task_distribution_horizon.falsifier: a horizon-free morphology claim that reverses when H is instantiated to the registered horizon (reuse amortization missed)

drift_regime_change.definition: Registered drift process Delta: E_t -> E_{t+1} distribution or adversarial regime-change schedule over H, including rate and which coordinates it perturbs.
drift_regime_change.parent: Grossberg stability-plasticity; EWC / continual learning drift parents (P4 ledger)
drift_regime_change.falsifier: a drift-free optimal morphology claimed stable under FREQUENT_SHIFT drift on which local-update morphologies provably revise cheaper (drift cost not booked)

recurrence_reuse_structure.definition: Recurrence map declaring which subtask patterns repeat across tasks (with frequency and horizon) and thus which PVR-3 amortization conditions are live; distinct from raw horizon count.
recurrence_reuse_structure.parent: HST-T05 macro amortization H_eff*dC_use > C_build+C_maint+C_rev; DreamCoder/Stitch library amortization
recurrence_reuse_structure.falsifier: a library/skill morphology claimed optimal on a FLAT recurrence ecology with no recurring pattern to amortize

noise_partial_observability.definition: Joint declaration of exogenous noise (label-flip, stochastic transition) and partial observability (which state variables are hidden under which condition), with latent/predictable-component separation.
noise_partial_observability.parent: Kearns 1998 SQ noise tolerance; POMDP belief-state parents
noise_partial_observability.falsifier: a noise-intolerant exact-consistency learner predicted optimal under LABEL_FLIP_HIGH without a noise-robust V

compositionality_symmetry_relational.definition: Registered compositionality depth, symmetry groups G acting on tasks, and relational schema (graph / binding structure) exposing which compositions are valid.
compositionality_symmetry_relational.parent: Fodor/Pylyshyn compositionality; SCAN / symmetry-equivariant learning literature
compositionality_symmetry_relational.falsifier: a holistic-code morphology claimed optimal on a DEEP_COMPOSITIONAL G-invariant product space at equal reuse where compositional sharing provably reduces description length

social_topology.definition: Where multiple agents exist, the social topology graph (who observes whom, who communicates with whom, bandwidth/latency on edges) and population structure (SINGLETON / FIXED_POPULATION / OPEN_ENDED) with the coordination obligation.
social_topology.parent: items 18/19 teaching-culture break-even n>1+S/(C-U); TOM-3 reliability probe pricing; collective decision literature
social_topology.falsifier: a teaching/culture morphology predicted optimal for SINGLETON population with no transmission recipient

embodiment_sensor_actuator.definition: Sensor/actuator constraints: what the agent can sense (resolution, modality, cost) and effect (actuator repertoire, embodiment dynamics, cost/latency), distinct from abstract O/A alphabets by declaring physical limits.
embodiment_sensor_actuator.parent: embodied cognition (Pfeifer & Bongard); physical-resource bridge parents (Landauer et al.)
embodiment_sensor_actuator.falsifier: a morphology requiring sensing/actuation precision beyond the registered embodiment limit yet claimed feasible without the embodiment coordinate

resource_prices_budgets.definition: Separate hard budget vector b (per-coordinate caps: desc/exec/upd/ver/rev) and price vector p (affine scalarization p.R) frozen prospectively when needed; budgets not scalarized post hoc.
resource_prices_budgets.parent: bounded rationality (Simon); resource-rational cognition; DEFINITIONS_V2_EXACT.md s5 affine-bound framework
resource_prices_budgets.falsifier: a morphology ordering that reverses under a registered price-vector flip that the claim did not condition on

verification_latency_cost.definition: Latency and charged cost of invoking V (delay between action and verdict, monetary/compute cost, false-adoption cost on error), per call and in aggregate over H.
verification_latency_cost.parent: verification-cost / decision-cost literature; PVR-3 certificate validity window
verification_latency_cost.falsifier: a verifier-gated morphology claimed to match a verifier-free morphology at equal reported cost without booking latency/false-adoption cost

information_acquisition_cost.definition: Charged cost of observation/query/probe acquisition (sample cost, probe cost, active-experiment cost) as distinct from exec/ver cost, with budget and price declared.
information_acquisition_cost.parent: Blackwell value of information; optimal experiment design (Lindley); TDA/GG12 acquisition family
information_acquisition_cost.falsifier: a probe policy claimed net-beneficial whose obligation-relevant uncertainty reduction does not exceed its booked acquisition cost (re-run TDA value check)

protected_splits.definition: Declared protected train/development/held-out splits: which world/task/identity partitions the construction/search has not seen before freeze, with sealing protocol and remint generator share.
protected_splits.parent: hold-out / cross-validation methodology; anti-story rule in ECOLOGY_CONTRACT_V1.json
protected_splits.falsifier: a held-out prediction that reproduces after leaking the held-out identities through an undeclared remint (label leakage)

equivalence_remint_rules.definition: Two ecologies are equivalent only under a labelled bijection (remint) preserving (O,A,F,V,p,b,H,Delta) up to renaming; a remint must be bijective on registered world/task alphabets and preserve observation/verification contracts by pullback. Any mapping that collapses distinct worlds or leaks oracle information is not a remint.
equivalence_remint_rules.parent: cryptographic remint / isomorphism methodology; anti-story rule: coordinates may not be selected after outcomes
equivalence_remint_rules.falsifier: a claimed ecology equivalence witnessed by a non-bijective or label-leaking map, or a held-out success that disappears under a disjoint bijective remint
